title: fix(plugin-report): format report displays in the display locale, not a literal en-US tag
body:
Fixes #10020

Clause-②: yes — `formatValue` is a published export of `@object-ui/plugin-report` (17.6.0, not private), so its signature is a public surface. This change stays on the non-breaking arm: the new locale is an OPTIONAL parameter, decided by the claiming seat before dispatch, not by the implementation.

## What was wrong

Five display paths in this package handed `Intl` the literal BCP-47 tag `en-US` — four branches of `formatValue` (`currency` / `currency_cny`, `currency_usd`, `percent`, the default thousand-separated branch) and the Excel cell formatter behind `exportExcelWithFormulas`. That is the exact tag `useDisplayLocale`'s contract in `@object-ui/i18n` names as the wrong answer, quoted here from the source I read on this branch's base:

> `'en'` — a concrete last resort rather than `undefined`. `undefined` would hand `Intl` the *machine's* locale, which is invisible in review and non-deterministic in CI; `'en'` at least fails the same way everywhere. Note this is `'en'`, not `'en-US'`: the point of objectui#4033 is that `en-US` is not the world's default.

The same package already resolved that channel three times in `DatasetReportRenderer.tsx`, so this was one package contradicting itself rather than a package unaware of the channel.

**The two shapes are kept apart, deliberately.** This card is the WRONG-TAG shape (`en-US` passed explicitly — the same wrong answer on every machine). The NO-TAG shape (a bare `toLocaleString()`, i.e. the machine's locale — non-deterministic in CI) is objectui#9909's, it is still present in this package's two HTML export-header lines, and it is untouched here.

## The parameter is OPTIONAL — why, and what that obliges

A required parameter would break every existing caller of a published export. That is a breaking change to a public signature and it is not this lane's to take; optional is purely additive, so everything that compiled before compiles after.

The cost of that choice is a leg that is still wrong when nobody passes a tag, and an optional parameter nobody passes is the same defect with a longer signature. So every in-repo call site now passes a resolved locale:

| Call site | Where the tag comes from |
|:--|:--|
| `ReportViewer` — the aggregation arm of `renderCellValue` | `useDisplayLocale()`, resolved once in the component |
| `ReportViewer` — the trailing arm of `renderCellValue` (no `type`, no `aggregation`) | same |
| `ReportViewer` — the summary card's `computeReportAggregation` value | same |
| `exportExcelWithFormulas` | its CALLER, through a new optional `locale` on the options bag it already takes |

**`LiveReportExporter` is not a component, so the honest answer is that its caller must pass one, and that is what this does.** It has no hook to read, and a report schema is the wrong carrier — a display locale is a property of the session, not of the authored report. It therefore takes the tag on its options bag. There is no in-repo caller of `exportExcelWithFormulas` today (it is consumed through the published package), so no in-repo call site of it had to change; its README example now passes a locale and the pin covers the parameter directly.

The default is `'en'` — the contract's own last resort, spelled once in a new `src/displayLocale.ts` rather than twice. It is deliberately neither `en-US` nor an absent tag.

**Not routed through `@object-ui/core`'s `formatDisplayNumber`, on purpose.** That would change the output convention beyond the locale tag (its own grouping and percent policy), and its malformed-tag retry drops the tag — which hands `Intl` the machine's locale, the other wrong answer this card must not introduce.

**A hazard the fix creates, and closes.** A hard-coded literal can never be malformed; a threaded tag arrives from tenant configuration and `en_US` (underscore) makes `Intl` throw RangeError — measured, and these calls sit inside a cell render. A malformed tag now degrades to the same last resort rather than taking the report down.

## Evidence

RED-before / GREEN-after on `packages/plugin-report/src/__tests__/reportDisplayLocale-10020.test.tsx`, with the file state verified by blob hash in the SAME command as each run. Every case pins the same value in de AND in en, so the assertion cannot pass by accident on a runner whose machine locale happens to match.

| Run | Tree state | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Pre-fix | `formatValue.ts` `18c12ccca`, `LiveReportExporter.ts` `bc0902c7e`, `ReportViewer.tsx` `72fb40de8`; four plus one `en-US` literals still on disk | 7 failed, 8 passed (15) |
| Post-fix | `formatValue.ts` `9606691ed`, `LiveReportExporter.ts` `bc5029092`, `ReportViewer.tsx` `b82ecb24c`, `displayLocale.ts` `478964547`; zero executable `en-US` literals, replacement symbol present as the control | 15 passed (15) |

**Prediction recorded before the run, and one of them was wrong.** The test file's header predicted the `formatValue` default-argument case would be green on both sides; it measured RED pre-fix, because its second assertion contrasts the default against de and pre-fix the de call does not move either. The header now records what was measured, not what was planned.

**Per-call-site ablation** — the three `ReportViewer` sites are pinned individually, not in aggregate. Reverting ONLY the aggregation arm (anchor hit once, blob `b82ecb24cf64` to `b5d164d4f0d0`, mutation proved on disk by the anchor count going 1 to 0) reds exactly one test, and the failure names the missing `1.234,5` while `9.876,5` and `2.468,5` are both present in the rendered output. Restore proved by content: on-disk blob back to `b82ecb24cf64`, equal to the HEAD blob, with `git diff HEAD` empty — never by an exit code.

**Doc-gate coverage control.** `check:doc-snippets` judges each README fence independently. An earlier draft added the locale in a SECOND fence, and that version is measured: exit 1, `TS2304: Cannot find name 'exportExcelWithFormulas'` at that block. Folding the option into the existing self-contained example makes it 673 of 673 judged, 0 failed. A deliberate type error in that block (`locale: 123`) reds the gate naming this README, which is the control proving the block is inside the judged population rather than silently skipped.

Gates run on the exact pushed tree `c2b2168a7`, with nothing unstaged:

| Gate | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-report/` | 18 files, 206 tests, all passed |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-report type-check` | exit 0 (its `tsconfig.test.json` leg lists the new test file — confirmed with `--listFiles`, control: an existing sibling test) |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | red before the changeset, green after — the level was read off the gate, not recalled |
| `check:doc-snippets` · `check:doc-types` · `check:readme-exports` | exit 0 (all three need a built tree; the packages they resolve against were built first) |
| `check:control-bytes` · `check:new-line-citations` · `check:changeset-claims` · `check:shell-escape-residue` · `check:phantom-deps` · `check:unused-deps` · `check:self-import` · `check:side-effects-array` · `check:test-path-roots` · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` · `check:doc-fences` · `check:i18n-keys` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-report lint` · `pnpm lint:coverage` · `check:lint-rule-coverage` | exit 0 — 0 errors (46 of 46 packages linted, 0 with outstanding errors) |

**Declared narrowing.** Lint was run as this package's own `eslint .` task, which is exactly the unit `pnpm lint` (`turbo run lint`) runs for it — complete for the package, not a sample inside it. Other packages' lint tasks were not run: no file outside `packages/plugin-report` and `.changeset/` changed, and this package's ESLint config is not type-aware across package boundaries, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The repo-wide sweep is CI's.

## Reading this diff

`src/displayLocale.ts` is new and small: the last-resort constant and the one malformed-tag-safe number formatter, so the policy is stated once instead of once per module — a package can only contradict a contract it states in more than one place.
